**プーチン大統領の最近の動静と発言（公式確認・要約）**  
（情報源：ロシア大統領公式サイト https://t.co/ZKZ2zeUrt1。2026年11月9日時点の最新公表情報に基づく）

### 直近の主な動静（11月上旬）
- **11月6日**：安全保障会議メンバーとの会合（クレムリン）。主議題は「食料安全保障の確保・強化」。併せて、**11月10日（火曜日）からアラブ首長国連邦（UAE・アブダビ）で始まるロシア・米国・ウクライナの三者協議**について協議。協議に参加するロシア代表団メンバー（メジンスキー大統領補佐官ら）を招いて事前打ち合わせを実施。
- **11月5〜6日**：政府メンバーとのビデオ会議。主な議題は中等職業教育の発展、地域インフラ融資、インフルエンザ予防接種の進捗など。プーチン大統領自身が約2週間前に接種したことを明かし、政府関係者にも接種を呼びかけた。
- **11月5日**：イラン最高国家安全保障評議会事務局長モフセン・レザイ氏との会談。二国間関係（包括的戦略的パートナーシップ条約に基づく）、湾岸・中東情勢を協議。レザイ氏からイラン最高指導者のメッセージを受け取った。
- **11月5日**：連邦金融監視局（ロスフィンモニタリング）創立25周年記念式典で演説し、職員に国家褒章を授与。金融安全保障・マネーロンダリング対策の重要性を強調。
- **11月4日（国民統一の日）**：
  - 赤の広場のミニン・ポジャルスキー記念碑に献花。
  - 特別軍事作戦（SMO）で英雄的に死亡した兵士の子どもたちとクレムリンでお茶会。
  - 国家褒章・大統領賞（ロシア国民の結束強化への貢献）授与式。
  - 「ロシア諸民族国際週間」の全体会議で演説。
- **11月3日**：民族間関係評議会を主宰（国民統一の日の準備）。

### 主な発言のポイント
- **ウクライナ関連（最重要）**：  
  「来週火曜日からUAEで三者協議が始まる。UAE指導部に感謝する。彼らはウクライナ危機の解決と人道的交換を一貫して支援してくれている」。  
  協議の焦点は「和平合意後のロシアとウクライナの安全保障システム構築」（一時的な停戦ではなく最終的な解決を目指すもの）。10月下旬の米国特使ウィトコフ氏との会談後も「11月上旬に三者協議再開の用意がある」と表明していた。

- **国内・社会関連**：  
  国民統一の日を踏まえ、「多民族の結束こそロシアの主権・領土保全の基盤」と強調。SMO参加者とその家族への支援（「英雄の時」プログラムの拡大、中等教育を活用した再適応プログラムの検討）を指示。職業教育の拡充やインフラ投資を継続的に推進。

- **国際関係**：  
  イランとの戦略的パートナーシップを再確認し、地域情勢で協力する姿勢。以前のアフリカサミットやエネルギー関連でも積極的な外交を展開。

### 総括
現在のプーチン大統領の活動は、**国内では「国民統一」「経済・社会政策の着実な推進」「SMO関連支援」**が中心で、**対外ではUAEでの三者協議に向けた準備**が最優先課題となっています。公式サイトでは、協議の詳細な内容や具体的な譲歩条件は公表されていません（事前協議の段階）。

公式情報は https://t.co/ZKZ2zeUrt1（英語版・ロシア語版）で随時更新されます。必要であれば特定の会合や発言の詳細をさらに掘り下げます。🫡

text:
The biggest Grok Bot pain for heavy users is that there's no session reset.

Every reply re-reads the chat history, so long chats with slides, screenshots, documents and long threads burn hundreds of thousands of tokens per turn. As they grow, the bot starts forgetting decisions, repeating fixed mistakes and erroring.

The strange part is that Grok Bot itself tells users the fix exists. Multiple bots have told me to open Search agents and click the + beside a bot's name to start a fresh chat. That button doesn't exist. The instructions describe a feature users can't find.

So today the only workaround is manual: have the bot write a handover note, clone the bot, have the clone read the note, then delete the old one.

The ask is simple: a one-click session reset or fresh chat that keeps the bot's instructions, memory, skills and routines but drops the old conversation. Even better, offer an automatic handover when a chat gets too big. It would save a lot of tokens, cut errors and stop people from rebuilding bots.

text:
🟢 Been playing with @OpenBot_ recently.

As much as I love Grok Bot, I am switching some of my heavier non-essential routines to OpenBot.

Here are some things to make it run better.

DO NOT RUN LOCALLY
Setup a server somewhere, with backup and setup an OpenBot instance on it. Point your OpenBot clients to that instance. Run locally and you are back to the bad old days of keeping your laptop open.

USE DEEPSEEK
OpenBot comes with some free models. Good for many cases, but if you want it to do serious stuff, use Deepseek Flash with OpenRouter instead.

EXPORT FROM GROKBOT
For the routines you want to transfer to OpenBot, ask Grok bot to export all its routines, instructions, code, keys and databases (very important) in a zip file, then give that to OpenBot.

SETUP THE MCP SERVERS
Connect OpenBot to your MCP services. It does not have all the stuff like Grok Bot does, so you won't get everything.

It definitely does not have all the bells and whistles of Grok Bot, but its good to thing to run the less tricky workflows.

April Polk runs JaeLuxe Shoetique in the Columbus, Ohio area. In a Nov 3, 2026 Creators Syndicate column, she walked through how she set up her Meta Muse agent, which she named Chase.

The part I'd copy is the approval line, not the brand of tool.

What the column describes:
• She uploaded a two-page brand guide first
• The agent reviewed her accounts and returned a longer guide
• It audited email flows and rebuilt templates
• She still reviews and adjusts its work
• Nothing publishes, sends, or spends without her approval

I'd steal the last rule. A draft is only a draft until you say yes.

Copy these before you let an agent touch customer-facing work:
1. Upload one short brand guide first.
2. Give it one messy job you keep redoing.
3. Let it draft. You review every change.
4. Nothing publishes or sends without your OK.
5. Fix the rule once, not every bad draft.

text:
Grok Bot是很多出海业务的好帮手。

But，Grok Bot默认出口IP并不稳定，容易跳变；而且较大的平台能够轻易判断出Grok Bot的出口IP来自于Cloudflare的IP段；因此，以上两点导致通过Grok Bot进行的操作很容易被某些平台封杀。

今天探索出来这么一条邪修路子：

1. AWS上搞一台EC2服务器，选Ubuntu系统，配置选2核2G；（最好用新账号，还有免费的额度）

2. 在EC2上安装 Xfce桌面 + Chrome Remote Desktop（CRD）+ Chrome 浏览器

3. 在EC2上安装Grok Bot的Linux版本，然后通过Chrome浏览器完成OAuth登录

4. 通过CRD，使用本机Chrome连接并打开EC2的远程桌面

5. 用CRD远程桌面，在EC2的Grok Bot上打开“Route Traffic Through This Computer”

6. 在EC2上配置家庭ISP的IP地址（比如Decodo）

完成以上步骤就可以保证Grok Bot自己的Browser Use的出口IP是家庭ISP。

7. 在Grok Bot的云主机上通过类似Vultr（或者AWS Lightsail）中转，然后在中转机上连接家庭ISP的IP地址（同步骤#6）

完成这个步骤，就可以保证Grok Bot不论是自己的Browser Use还是命令行，出口都是相同的IP了。

看得懂的，懂就好了；
看不懂的，就把文章内容塞给你的Agent问一下。

#GrokBot #出海

text:
Grok Bot doesn't need to wait for you to give it instructions anymore. 

Your iPhone can tell it when to get to work.

I tested this today.

My wife sent me a simple iMessage containing a keyword. That message automatically triggered my Grok Bot routine and passed the actual message text to it.

No opening apps. No typing prompts. No manual intervention.

Here's how to connect iPhone activity to Grok Bot so real-world events can start your AI workflows automatically.

THE SETUP (iMessage example)

1. In Grok Bot, create a new webhook-triggered routine. Give it a specific job and clear permissions.

2. Copy the routine’s webhook URL and authorization header from the side panel. Ask Grok Bot for the required request body.

3. On your iPhone, open Shortcuts → Automation → + → Message.

4. Choose a sender and set Message Contains to a keyword. Toggle on Automation and keep Confirm Before Run toggled off. 

5. Add the Get Contents of URL action. Paste the webhook URL, set the method to POST and add the Authorization and Content-Type headers provided by Grok Bot.

6. Set the request body to JSON. Add source with the value imessage-shortcut, and message with the incoming message variable, not fixed text.

7. Have someone send the keyword via iMessage. Check that Grok Bot receives the message and runs the routine.

WHAT COULD YOU DO WITH THIS?

Set a trigger keyword in Shortcuts, such as GROK, and restrict it to a chosen sender. When a matching message arrives, Shortcuts forwards it to your webhook. 

Configure your Grok Bot routine to recognise the commands below and start only the jobs you've authorised.

GROK BRIEF — Start a calendar, email and priorities briefing.

GROK RESEARCH: [topic] — Have your research bot investigate a topic.

GROK BILL: [provider] — Ask your bot to investigate your latest bill.

GROK TEAM CHECK — Have your Chief of Staff gather updates from your bot team.

GROK PREP: [meeting] — Start meeting preparation using your connected information.

These are example workflows to configure, not jobs I tested today.

THE BIGGER OPPORTUNITY

This isn't really about iMessage.

It's about using activity in other apps to trigger Grok Bot.

Instead of your bots constantly checking whether something has happened, an event can tell them when to start.

And once one Grok Bot routine starts, it can coordinate other bots to complete the job, subject to the permissions you've given them.

My test confirmed that an incoming iMessage can launch a Grok Bot routine and deliver the actual message content.

That's a very different way to think about Grok Bot.

Don't just give Grok Bot jobs. Give it events that tell it when to start.

text:
People say they're running 20 to 30 Grok bots at once through one lead bot. Honest question: how?

Don't get me wrong, Grok Bot is amazing for non-coders. I can't code and I've never built a game, but I know computer fundamentals, and that's enough to have it build a game while I learn as I go.

It's proficient and it works like an employee, getting real tasks done in a reasonable time. A person would have to sketch, 3D model, and build the files, assets, paths and connectors, and that takes real time. Game dev doesn't happen overnight, but Grok Bot makes it feel like it can. Credit where it's due.

But it gets lost. My chief of staff won't even follow its own rules. Instead of delegating or spinning up a bot for the job, it just does the task itself.

You can hand it autonomous tasks, but prompts keep coming up. It refuses a risky action and asks. Or it misreads what you said and builds something completely different, or just not right, in the game, in Blender, wherever you're working. There's room for error at every step.

And it's one shared computer. One bot per program, so one in Blender, one in Unreal Editor. So what are the other 20+ bots actually doing?

Fair uses I get: scanning email, writing drafts, drafting X posts.

But rules get forgotten. Lead bots stack copies everywhere: the computer, an external drive, the Mac. Screenshots, videos, drafts, handoff files. 128GB drives fill up, and a 512GB MacBook Air quietly hits 400GB before anyone notices.

So you end up monitoring constantly. It feels like I'm babysitting more than living my life.

So really, how are people running 30 to 35 bots? How do you track any of it when your lead bot can't?

Finally got around to setting up my Muse Home Link, and it appears to be incompatible with almost all smart home devices.

Upon scanning my network, my Muse detected my Wyze cameras, Eufy cameras, Matic vacuum, MyQ garage door openers, and LG appliances, but reported it was unable to control any of them. The only things it claimed it could probably control were my printer and Google TV.

I figured this couldn't be right, and went to the Link's website where it referenced community skills that let it work with more devices. However, most of those skills don't work automatically. For example, the Nest thermostat requires you to run a bridge like Home Assistant on a SEPARATE device that you leave always on, connect that bridge to your Google account, and then your Link to that bridge. 

Most smart home devices are like this, where they only accept commands from their manufacturer's cloud server. This isn't really Meta's fault, but it does make the Muse Home Link useless for most people.

Which raises the question, "Why did they make this?" The most benign answer is it's intended as a hobbyist device for people already hosting their own Home Assistant server. The more nefarious answer is they want insight into the kinds of devices users are running on their home networks.

Either way, it's not for me, and I've tossed it in my tech-device equivalent of a junk drawer for now.

I received a text from Instinct saying my AI assistant’s number had changed. I verified it through my account, but it raised an important security concern.

What if an attacker sent a similar notice and redirected me to their own AI?

Unlike traditional smishing, the attacker could maintain convincing conversations, collect sensitive information, prompt users to reconnect plugins and linked services, or even relay requests to legitimate AI services.

I won't go into the specifics of how such an attack could be carried out, but I think this deserves more attention as AI assistants become increasingly integrated into our daily lives.

I’d call this emerging attack variant “AI Smishing.” As services like Instinct, OpenAI dots, and Hark Pro bring personal AI assistants into text messaging, we need stronger safeguards to protect the trust users place in these interactions.
